metadata.note: The Hartford & New Haven Railroad's New Haven-Springfield line, once the main New York-Boston rail route, and the historical line underlying Amtrak's Hartford Line and Valley Flyer. Route geometry is taken from the modern Amtrak route's own GTFS-sourced alignment for this corridor (see amtrak.geojson), since the historical train ran the same physical line; where the historical train ran beyond or differently from today's Amtrak route, that is described in the segment notes. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not from real timetables.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (Hartford and New Haven Railroad, New Haven-Springfield Line), nhrhta.org
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.ownership_split_audit: 2026-10-14: CLAUDE.md Rule 4. The single feature drew the line's whole 1839-2025 history under the Hartford and New Haven's name. Split at the 1872 merger into the New York, New Haven and Hartford: hnh-new-haven-springfield keeps 1839-1872; the new feature nynhh-new-haven-springfield (identical geometry, colour pulled from nynhh-new-haven-line) carries 1872-1969. The 1976-2025 segment (Amtrak era, still labelled and coloured H&NH) was dropped, not split: amtrak.geojson amtrak-41042 'Amtrak: Hartford Line' has identical geometry and already draws 1971-2025, so an Amtrak copy would be a duplicate. That dropped segment's note also said 'Conrail from April 1 1976, then Amtrak', which is wrong for passenger service - Amtrak took over intercity passenger trains on 1 May 1971; Conrail ran none here.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Penn Central ran passenger service on this line from the 1969 New Haven inclusion until Amtrak Day, 1 May 1971; that 1969-1971 gap is not drawn by any feature. Adding a Penn Central (#1A1A1A) segment would need a timetable check.

segments.note: The Hartford & New Haven Railroad built north from New Haven, opening its first segment in 1838 and reaching Hartford in Dec 1839. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
sources: Segment-level: this segment's own note carries the citation for its dates and service. Supporting references for the line:
Wikipedia (Hartford and New Haven Railroad, New Haven-Springfield Line), nhrhta.org

segments.note: Extended to Springfield, MA in 1844 (via its Hartford & Springfield subsidiary), forming the first all-rail route between Boston and New Haven, with Long Island Sound steamships completing the link to New York. It carried most of the New York-Boston traffic until the Thames River bridge at New London opened in 1889, even after the coastal Shore Line was finished in 1858. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

properties.geometry_quality: Not traced from OSM: geometry is the 30-vertex Amtrak GTFS shape shared with amtrak.geojson amtrak-41042 (Hartford Line), so curves are coarse. Length 61.4 mi against the documented ~62 mi New Haven-Springfield line, a close fit. Draws today's alignment; any 19th/20th-century realignments or station relocations on the corridor have not been checked.
